skill_traces.query:
Gina: Hey Jon, what's been up? Some pretty cool stuff happened since we talked. I have acquired some new unique pieces for my store.
Jon: Congrats on your store, Gina! Happy for you! It looks sick - is it a unique piece you're selling?
Gina: Thanks! This hoodie isn't for sale, it's from my own collection. I made a limited edition line last week to show off my style and creativity - it was tough but worth it!
Jon: What gave you the idea?
Gina: This design reminds me of the grit it takes to stand out and face challenges.
Jon: That's awesome, Gina! Yesterday I chose to go to networking events to make things happen. It's been tough but I'm staying determined and focused.
Gina: Way to go, Jon! Attending those networking events takes guts and drive. Keep it up!
Jon: Thanks! It's been tough going since I lost my job, but I'm sure investing my time in my business will pay off eventually. I really appreciate your help.
Gina: No worries, Jon! You got this! Let me know if you need anything.
Jon: Your help matters to me. I am writing all my plans down.
Gina: Nice work! Tracking your plans and goals is key. It's like a picture of all your progress.
Jon: Thanks, Gina! Seeing my goals written down on paper really helps keep me motivated and focused on what I have to do. I know it won't be easy, but I'm sure it'll pay off. Thanks for the support!
Gina: No worries, Jon! When things get rough, keep persevering and keep working hard. You'll get there! Don't quit!
Jon: Thanks, Gina! That sign reminds me to never give up, however hard things get. I'll keep going!
Gina: Believe in yourself and keep going. You can do it!
Jon: Thanks! I'm feeling confident and won't give up. Your support means a ton to me.

selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.
selected.rerank_reason: Jon mentions his goal of investing time in his business and tracking his plans, which are explicit goals and intended impacts. This skill is applicable for capturing these goals and their impact.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.

nearby_not_selected.name: Record Specific Product Type in Creation Events
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when creating or updating a memory about someone making a product line, collection, or series, and the message names the specific item type.
content: When creating or updating an event memory about someone creating or making a product line, collection, or series, always resolve coreferences in the message and record the concrete product/item type (e.g., hoodies) that the line consists of.
Do not use generic terms like 'a line' or 'a collection' when the message specifies what the line or collection contains.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.
